purpose: Reference-derived semantic upper-garment grammars. No source pixels or coordinates are stored.
referenceSafety: Research-only abstraction; generated work must not reproduce source sprites, logos, characters, or exact costume layouts.

grammars.silhouette: close, straight torso with quiet shoulders
grammars.necklineCollar: small crew or shallow V; no collar mass
grammars.sleeveBehavior: native short sleeves; sleeve value follows body fabric
grammars.hemWaist: clean normal hem; optional tucked cue
grammars.layering: none or a very small undershirt edge
grammars.frontGrammar: neck binding is the structural focal point; torso remains one readable mass
grammars.sideGrammar: retain neck depth and sleeve edge; omit front-only motif
grammars.backGrammar: quiet back with neck binding and optional upper-back mark
commonFailures: using a center stripe as fake construction

grammars.silhouette: boxier torso with dropped visual shoulder and looser lower edge
grammars.necklineCollar: wide crew
grammars.sleeveBehavior: native short sleeve with body-colored shoulder extension
grammars.frontGrammar: width and neck openness carry identity before graphics
grammars.sideGrammar: show broader body mass and sleeve projection
grammars.backGrammar: preserve boxy width; graphic may disappear or become a small echo

grammars.silhouette: neat fitted or regular torso
grammars.necklineCollar: small structured collar around a short opening
grammars.sleeveBehavior: short native sleeve with optional bound edge

grammars.sideGrammar: collar projects behind neck; placket vanishes
grammars.backGrammar: collar back is the dominant cue
commonFailures: full placket turning it into a button shirt
crew neck turning it into a tee
